segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Good morning everyone, let's get started with today's quarterly review.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Morning KY. I've prepared the metrics dashboard — we can walk through it section by section.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Perfect. Starting with Q3 revenue: we hit 94% of target, which is a solid result given the market headwinds we discussed last month.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Agreed. The slight shortfall came from two enterprise deals that slipped to Q4. Both are now closed, so we expect Q4 to make up the delta.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Good. On the product side, the new onboarding flow went live in week 11. Activation rates improved by 18% in the first two weeks.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: That was a team effort — the UX redesign and the backend optimisation happened in parallel, which was risky but paid off.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Let's talk about the support queue. We're still running at 48-hour median resolution. The target is 24 hours. What's blocking that?

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Two things: first, tier-1 agents don't have access to the new diagnostic tool yet — IT is rolling that out this week. Second, we have three open headcount positions. Until they're filled, throughput stays capped.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Understood. Let's flag the headcount issue to HR today. I'll also sync with IT to confirm the diagnostic tool rollout date.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: On engineering velocity: sprint completion rate is at 87%. Two stories were blocked by a third-party API regression that was outside our control.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: That's acceptable. What's the remediation plan for the API dependency?

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: We're adding a circuit-breaker and a local cache for the affected endpoint. Estimated completion by end of next sprint — so two weeks from today.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Good mitigation. Shifting to people topics — the engagement survey closed last Friday. Participation was 91%, which is our highest ever.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: The top three themes were: flexible working arrangements, clearer career progression paths, and more cross-team collaboration opportunities. We'll present the detailed results at next month's all-hands.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Before all-hands, I'd like each team lead to draft a one-page action plan responding to the themes relevant to their area. Can you own the engineering response?

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Absolutely. I'll have a draft by end of next week.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Great. Let me summarise the action items: one, HR to be notified about open headcount; two, IT sync on diagnostic rollout; three, circuit-breaker implementation in two weeks; four, TF to draft engineering engagement response.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: I'll log all of those in Jira and send a follow-up email today. Anything else before we close?

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Just one more thing — we've been invited to present at the industry conference in November. I think it's a good visibility opportunity. TF, would you be willing to co-present on the onboarding flow case study?

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: I'd love to. That's a great story to share externally. Happy to prepare the slide deck. Can we block two hours next week to align on messaging?

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Done. I'll send a calendar invite right after this call. Alright, I think we're good. Thanks everyone for a productive session.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Thanks KY. Talk soon.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: One more topic I want to circle back on: infrastructure costs. We're over budget by 12% this quarter.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Yes, the main drivers are the data pipeline scaling event in August and the increased storage for the new audit logging requirements.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Are there short-term optimisation opportunities without impacting reliability?

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Two quick wins: rightsizing the dev cluster saves roughly 15% of compute costs, and enabling S3 intelligent tiering on the archive bucket cuts storage by about 30%. Combined that erases maybe 8% of the overage.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Let's execute both next sprint. Add them to the backlog with a P1 label.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Will do. For the remaining 4% gap, I'll model two scenarios and bring options to the next steering committee.

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: Perfect. Alright, now we're truly done. Have a great rest of the day.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: You too. Bye!

segments.speaker: KY
segments.text: This sentence was generated much too quickly to be real speech and should be flagged as a potential hallucination.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Thank you for watching.

segments.speaker: TF
segments.text: Thank you for watching.
